name: Banasura Sagar Dam
tagline: Boating, island hopping and lakeside eco‑stays — best in crisp winter weather
summary: India's largest earthen dam with seasonal islands and boating on a scenic reservoir beneath the Banasura Hills. Winter (Oct–Mar) gives the clearest mornings for boats, photography and lakeside…
description: Banasura Sagar is a large earthen reservoir near Padinjarathara in Wayanad; it is widely described as India’s largest earth‑fill dam and a major scenic landmark in the district. ([keralatourism.org](https://www.keralatourism.org/routes-locations/banasura-sagar-dam/id/1472))

The dam’s reservoir creates a scattering of seasonal islands and hillocks that attract boaters, kayakers and small lakeside camps; organised boating (speedboats, pedal boats and similar services) operates from the visitor area under local hydel/tourism management. ([keralahydeltourism.com](https://www.keralahydeltourism.com/attractions))

Visitors come for short boat trips and island hopping, sunrise kayaking and nearby eco‑stays or campsite experiences that use the dam’s shoreline; access to islands depends on water level and permissions, so confirm availability before you travel. ([wayanadbook.com](https://www.wayanadbook.com/news/banasura-sagar-dam-asias-largest-earthen-dam-opens-new-boating-zone))
highlights: Largest earthen dam in India with Banasura Hills backdrop.
Boating options: speedboats, pedal boats and kayak/sunrise tours (seasonal).
Seasonal islands and designated lakeside/island camps offered by local operators.
Clear winter mornings (Oct–Mar) give best light for photos and calm water.
Good base for short treks (Banasura Hill) and nearby Wayanad attractions.

sections.heading: Background
body: Built across the Karamanathodu tributary in Padinjarathara, the Banasura Sagar reservoir is both a functional irrigation/hydel project and a widely visited scenic spot; state tourism pages and district guides list it as a signature Wayanad attraction. ([keralatourism.org](https://www.keralatourism.org/routes-locations/banasura-sagar-dam/id/1472))

The reservoir’s water levels change with the monsoon and irrigation demand; when levels fall the exposed hillocks form small islands that operators sometimes include in organised boat trips and permitted camping activities. ([wayanadbook.com](https://www.wayanadbook.com/news/banasura-sagar-dam-asias-largest-earthen-dam-opens-new-boating-zone))

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Take a short speedboat or pedal‑boat trip from the visitor jetty for island views and panorama of the forested Banasura Hills; some operators also advertise sunrise kayaking and guided nature walks along the dam bund. ([keralahydeltourism.com](https://www.keralahydeltourism.com/attractions))

If you prefer staying near the water, several lakeside camps and resorts in the Padinjarathara/Kalpetta area offer tents or cottages with views of the reservoir — many package boat rides and bonfire nights during the dry season. Confirm whether island camping is included and whether local permits are needed. ([wayanadn.com](https://www.wayanadn.com/banasura-sagar-dam-boating-rates-timings/))

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Best time: October–March for cool, clear mornings and stable boating; monsoon (June–September) brings high water and many activities close or run limited services. Always confirm boat and island access on the day of travel. ([keralatourism.org](https://www.keralatourism.org/routes-locations/banasura-sagar-dam/id/1472))

Getting around: Padinjarathara / the dam is around 20–22 km from Kalpetta and is reachable by road from Mananthavady and Kalpetta by taxi or local bus; parking and visitor facilities are centred at the hydel tourism/boating area. Bookings for organised hydel boating are handled via Kerala Hydel Tourism or local operators. ([keralatourism.org](https://www.keralatourism.org/routes-locations/banasura-sagar-dam/id/1472))

latest.text: A new boating zone and expanded activities (sunrise kayaking, guided bund walks and designated island camping/campfire areas) were announced for the reservoir’s visitor area; island access remains conditional on water level and permissions.

visitorInfo.bestTime: October to March (clear, cool mornings — best for boating and island views)
visitorInfo.howToReach: Drive or taxi from Kalpetta (about 20–22 km) or Mananthavady; regular state buses serve Padinjarathara and local taxis take visitors to the hydel/boating area. Confirm boat schedules with the hydel‑tourism desk before you go. ([keralatourism.org](https://www.keralatourism.org/routes-locations/banasura-sagar-dam/id/1472))
etiquette: Confirm boating, kayak and island camping availability on the day — water level and permissions change seasonally. ([wayanadbook.com](https://www.wayanadbook.com/news/banasura-sagar-dam-asias-largest-earthen-dam-opens-new-boating-zone))
Bring layers for cool winter dawns, sunscreen and a waterproof bag for cameras; carry cash as small operators may not accept cards.

Respect local rules: use only designated camping areas and follow guidance from boat crews — open fires on islands may be restricted. ([wayanadbook.com](https://www.wayanadbook.com/news/banasura-sagar-dam-asias-largest-earthen-dam-opens-new-boating-zone))
Avoid the monsoon months (June–September) when boating/island access is commonly suspended or limited.
